extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys preparing/submitting USPTO patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the required parts, permitted formats, and examiner treatment of amendments, new matter, sequence listings, large tables, computer program listings, and read-only optical disc or electronic submissions to the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to New Matter (Form Paragraph 7.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132(a) because it introduces new matter into the disclosure; applicant is required to cancel the new matter in reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.28. Note that 35 U.S.C. 132(a) states no amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure. Examiner Note: No amendment is permitted in a provisional application after it receives a filing date. Do not use this form paragraph in reissue applications (use form paragraph 14.22.01 instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of New Matter by Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: When objecting, identify the added material that is not supported by the original disclosure by page and line numbers and provide an appropriate explanation of the position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation should address any applicant statements supporting possession in the specification as filed and include any unresolved questions that raise doubt as to possession of the claimed invention at the time of filing. If new matter is entered into the claims or affects the claims, treat the new matter as part of claimed subject matter for other rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter Consequences for Claims (35 U.S.C. 112 / written description)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the new matter has been entered into the claims or affects the scope of the claims, the affected claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph) for reciting elements without support in the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is added to the claims, or affects them, make a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) using form paragraph 7.31.01. If new matter is added only to a claim, do not use Form Paragraph 7.28 (which is for specification amendments) — instead reject the claim using 7.31.01. New matter must be considered part of the claimed subject matter for purposes of any other appropriate prior art or 35 U.S.C. 112 rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples/Forms of New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter includes addition of wholly unsupported subject matter, adding specific percentages or compounds after a broader original disclosure, omission of a step from a method, a new structural formula, or a new use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Wertheim and MPEP § 2163.05 for guidance on when added specifics (percentages/compounds) constitute new matter. Use MPEP §§ 2163.06 and 2163.07 to determine whether an amendment adds new matter and the relationship to 35 U.S.C. 112(a). Determine whether added characteristics (chemical/physical properties) are inherent and therefore do not introduce new matter (see MPEP § 2163.07(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter in Drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed but is not shown in the drawing, the claim is not rejected but applicant is required to add it to the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement drawings containing new matter should not be entered; explain corrections necessary to obtain entry of the drawings using form paragraph 6.37. See MPEP § 608.01(l) for drawings guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Amendment Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment present on the filing date (filed with the application) is part of the original disclosure; a preliminary amendment filed after the filing date is not part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after Sept 21, 2004, the Office will automatically treat any preliminary amendment under 37 CFR 1.115(a)(1) that is present on the filing date as part of the original disclosure. Applicants are strongly encouraged to avoid submitting preliminary amendments (incorporate desired amendments into the specification) to minimize Office burden and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review/Appeal of Examiner's Holding of New Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the new matter is confined to amendments to the specification, review of the examiner's requirement for cancelation is by petition; where alleged new matter is introduced into or affects the claims (necessitating their rejection), the matter is appealable and should not be considered on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP § 2163.06 for additional guidance on petition vs appeal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Submission Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted electronically to the Office must be formatted and transmitted in compliance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Patent Center and USPTO electronic filing system technical and formatting rules; see the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Types Permitted on Read-Only Optical Disc
rubrics_metrics.description: The following documents may be submitted on a read-only optical disc in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e): a Computer Program Listing Appendix (§ 1.96(c)); a Sequence Listing or Sequence Listing XML (§ 1.821(c) or § 1.831(a)); or Large Tables (§ 1.58(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read-only optical disc submissions must conform to paragraph (e) requirements and related parts for each document type (e.g., compression rules and format-specific sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-Only Optical Disc Technical and Media Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A read-only optical disc must be finalized and in conformance with ISO 9660, and must be one of: CD–ROM, CD–R, DVD–R, or DVD+R. CD-RW, DVD-RW, and DVD+RW are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting to non-rewritable media ensures longevity and integrity; use DVD-R/DVD+R and non-self-extracting compression to reduce physical media count. If a user submits electronic copies that exceed size limits on discs, recommended to submit via Priority Mail Express or hand delivery on date of corresponding electronic filing if wishing disc copy to be part of the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read-Only Disc File Format and Viewer Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For Large Tables, Computer Program Listing Appendix, Sequence Listing, or CRF of a Sequence Listing, contents of each read-only optical disc must be in ASCII plain text; for a Sequence Listing XML, contents must be in XML format and encoded using UTF-8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No non-ASCII characters or proprietary file formats permitted for ASCII submissions; text viewer recommended. Each text file must have a file name with a '.txt' extension; each XML file must have a '.xml' extension. Compression, if used, must follow the applicable section (e.g., § 1.58 for Large Tables, § 1.96 for Computer Program Listing Appendix, § 1.824 for Sequence Listing, § 1.834 for Sequence Listing XML). See WIPO ST.26 character definitions for permitted characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal Letter Contents for Read-Only Optical Discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must be accompanied by a transmittal letter including specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal letter must include: first-named inventor (if known); title of the invention; attorney docket/file reference number (if applicable); application number and filing date (if known); operating system used to produce the disc; and file(s) contained on the disc including file name, size in bytes, and date of creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling Requirements for Read-Only Optical Discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each read-only optical disc must have a label permanently affixed thereto on which certain information is hand-printed or typed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label must include first-named inventor (if known); title of the invention; attorney docket/file reference number (if applicable); application number and filing date (if known); date on which data were recorded on the disc; disc order (e.g., '1 of X') if multiple discs are submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreadable Files and Disc Non-Return Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a file is unreadable it will be treated as not having been submitted; read-only optical discs will not be returned to the applicant and may not be retained as part of the patent application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unreadable, a notice will be issued to require a compliant submission. Plan submissions to avoid unreadable formats and to retain backup copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of Disc Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to the information on a read-only optical disc must be by way of a replacement read-only optical disc, in compliance with the applicable sections for Large Tables, Computer Program Listing Appendix, Sequence Listing, or Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow § 1.58(g) for Large Tables, § 1.96(c)(5) for Computer Program Listing Appendix, § 1.825(b) for Sequence Listing/CRF, and § 1.835(b) for Sequence Listing XML when submitting replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Size Fee—Read-Only Optical Disc Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application component submitted in part on a read-only optical disc, each three kilobytes of content submitted on the disc shall be counted as a sheet of paper for application size fee determination (with specified exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded from this determination are ASCII plain text files or XML files that contain: any Sequence Listing or CRF of a Sequence Listing in compliance with § 1.821(c) or (e), any Sequence Listing XML in compliance with § 1.831(a), or any Computer Program Listing Appendix in compliance with § 1.96(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Size Fee—Electronic Filing System Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application submitted in whole or in part via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, the paper size equivalent will be considered 75% of the number of sheets of paper present in the specification and drawings when entered into the Office records after being rendered by the electronic filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded from this determination are ASCII plain text files or XML files (as applicable) that contain any Sequence Listing or CRF of a Sequence Listing, any Sequence Listing XML, or any Computer Program Listing Appendix that are in compliance with the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing File Submission Options (transitional rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sequence Listing under 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 may be submitted as an ASCII plain text file only in applications filed before July 1, 2022; Sequence Listing XML applies for applications filed on or after July 1, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Sequence Listing is filed as a PDF or on paper without an ASCII text file in certain national-stage situations, a separate Computer Readable Form (CRF) is required. Checker software for compliance with 37 CFR 1.824 is available from the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML Requirement (apps filed on/after July 1, 2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed on or after July 1, 2022 that contain nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosures must provide sequence information as a Sequence Listing XML submitted as an XML file complying with 37 CFR 1.831–1.834.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence Listing XML must be filed via Patent Center or on read-only optical disc, encoded in UTF-8, and comply with the WIPO ST.26 XML requirements. Applicable filing date rules mirror other filing date determinations per 37 CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements Required When Adding or Replacing Sequence Listings After Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding or replacing a Sequence Listing (ASCII or XML) after the filing date via the USPTO electronic filing system, specific accompanying statements and requests are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding (37 CFR 1.825(a)) include: request to have amendment entered using incorporation by reference (if desired), a statement that submission does not include new matter (1.825(a)(4)), and a statement identifying the basis for the amendment with specific references to parts of the application as originally filed (1.825(a)(3)). When replacing (1.825(b) or 1.835(b)) include: statement of no new matter, statement identifying basis for amendments with specific references to original parts (spec., claims, drawings), and statement identifying location of deletions/replacements/additions (1.825(b)(3)-(5) / 1.835(b)(2)-(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Size Fee—Large Sequence Listing Fee Tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sequence Listing in electronic form or Sequence Listing XML of 300 MB–800 MB filed under 35 U.S.C. 111 or 371 will be subject to the fee in § 1.21(o)(1); any submission that exceeds 800 MB will be subject to the fee in § 1.21(o)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check applicable fee schedule and ensure large sequence listing files are accompanied by appropriate fee payments when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: File Size Limits for Electronic Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Size limits for electronic submissions via the USPTO patent electronic filing system: 100 MB limit for Sequence Listing (ASCII or XML); for nearly all other file types, 25 MB limit (including ASCII plain text files for Computer Program Listing Appendix and Large Tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files above these size limits must be submitted on read-only optical discs. 'Large Tables' or 'Computer Program Listing Appendix' files can be split into multiple files ≤ 25 MB, with filenames indicating order (e.g., '1 of X'). Sequence Listing ASCII files exceeding 100 MB cannot be divided and must be submitted on read-only optical discs. If submitting on discs, consider Priority Mail Express or hand delivery concurrently with electronic filing to ensure disc copy is treated as part of the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed ASCII/Text and XML Submission Practices and Incorporation by Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain document types may be submitted as ASCII text files or XML via the electronic filing system, provided the specification contains a separate-paragraph incorporation by reference identifying the file name, date of creation, and size in bytes (with specific international-stage exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document types include: Computer Program Listing Appendix (37 CFR 1.96(c)), Sequence Listing (37 CFR 1.821(c)), Large Tables (37 CFR 1.58(c)), and Sequence Listing XML (37 CFR 1.831(a)). A CRF of a Sequence Listing must be filed as ASCII plain text and still requires an incorporation-by-reference statement because the CRF is not part of the specification. Form paragraphs 6.61.02 and 6.71.02 may be used to indicate the need to add or amend an incorporation by reference statement for text files submitted via electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and Structure of Application Elements (37 CFR 1.77)
rubrics_metrics.description: The elements of the application, if applicable, should appear in the following order: utility application transmittal form; fee transmittal form; application data sheet (§ 1.76); specification; drawings; inventor's oath or declaration. The specification should include sections (if applicable) in this order: title; cross-reference to related applications; statement regarding federally sponsored research; names of parties to a joint research agreement; incorporation by reference paragraph for ASCII/XML files; statement regarding prior disclosures; background; brief summary; brief description of drawings; detailed description; claims; abstract; and Sequence Listing (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text of the specification sections should be preceded by a section heading in uppercase and without underlining or bold type. See § 1.77(b) and related subsections for details on what to include (e.g., incorporation by reference statements for ASCII/XML files).
